name: Monzo
summary: Monzo is a UK digital bank with 15.2 million customers, and is reportedly in talks to be acquired by Nubank for £8–10 billion.
overview: Monzo is a UK-licensed digital bank offering current accounts, savings, loans and business banking through its app.
bull_case: Profitable growth and a large UK customer base make Monzo attractive to an acquirer or public investors.
bear_case: The reported price is high relative to profit, and international expansion has been slow.
latest_round: October 2024: £4.5B employee share sale; Nubank takeover talks reported

intelligence.description: Monzo is a UK-licensed digital bank offering current accounts, savings, loans and business banking through its app.
company: Monzo was founded in London in 2015 and has grown into one of the UK's largest digital banks, with 15.2 million customers. Its latest annual results showed revenue of £1.7 billion, up 39%, and statutory pre-tax profit of £87.3 million. Diana Layfield became CEO in October 2025.

Monzo was last valued at £4.5 billion in an October 2024 employee share sale. In September 2026 Sky News and Bloomberg reported that Brazil's Nubank was in talks to buy Monzo for £8–10 billion, roughly double that valuation.
intelligence.why_it_matters: Monzo is the UK's most prominent fintech, and a Nubank deal would be one of the largest fintech acquisitions and a benchmark for neobank valuations.

changed.text: An employee share sale values Monzo at £4.5B.
Nubank is reported to be in talks to buy Monzo for £8–10B.

takeaways: A deal would value Monzo at about twice its last price.
It is profitable, but margins are thin relative to revenue.
Growth outside the UK remains unproven.
Talks may not lead to a deal.
